newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown to scrap dividend credit, not MIRAS -FT.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown to scrap dividend credit, not MIRAS -FT.

text.p: Britain's chancellor of the exchequer (finance minister), Gordon Brown, is considering abolishing a tax credit on dividend payments which could raise up to five billion stg from pension funds and other tax-exempt institutions, the Financial Times newspaper said.
The newspaper said in its Monday edition that the move on tax credits and a windfall tax on the profits of privatised companies would form the centerpieces of Brown's budget next month.
The newspaper, citing senior ministers, said Brown's budget would not abolish mortgage interest tax relief (MIRAS) or make major changes to personal tax, as many reports have speculated.
The Financial Times said a move to abolish the 20 percent tax credit on dividend payments could deprive pension funds of annual income of around 3.5 billion stg.
It said Brown had been advised the tax advantage was partly responsible for British companies' relatively high dividends and low investment.
Brown said last week his first budget would centre on a welfare-to-work programme to cut unemployment. He said the new Labour government would seek higher corporate investment.
